description: A server issues sequential task IDs and answers tasks/get for any of them. Because a task ID may be used as a bearer token for stored state, low-entropy IDs are directly readable by a third party.

fixture.observedBehavior: server returns the task record for a caller that does not own it

expected.signal: sequential / low-entropy task identifiers, and a tasks/get answered without an authorization check against the caller
expected.rationale: ext-tasks §Security Considerations: servers MUST generate task IDs with sufficient entropy that a third party cannot enumerate or guess them, and MUST perform authentication and authorization checks on each task-related request.

benignControl.observedBehavior: server returns the task record to its owner

provenance: synthetic — ext-tasks specification/2026-07-28/tasks.md §Security Considerations. NOTE: there is deliberately no tasks/list in this revision, so no enumeration variant exists; see docs/SPEC-VERIFICATION-2026-07-28.md, Correction 2.
